entries.proposition: Genre: a narrative review whose stated hypothesis is that intermittent hypoxia from obstructive sleep apnoea is the link to epilepsy; no patient or animal data are generated, and WWOX is not named.
entries.snippet: Intermittent hypoxia caused by OSAS, especially during REM sleep, might play crucial role in the pathogenesis of epilepsy.

entries.proposition: Search method is a keyword list over four databases up to a date, with no inclusion rule, appraisal or counts.
entries.snippet: The search was limited to English-language publications.

entries.proposition: Clinical evidence for the CPAP route is a 1994 case series and a 2022 study: the text says 7 patients and then reports 4 of 5, so its own denominators differ.
entries.snippet: showing that 4/5 of the patients significantly reduced the frequency of seizures after positive pressure ventilation

entries.proposition: The text states seizures were controlled when hypoxia was corrected by CPAP, citing one source, and calls it confirmation of the link.
entries.snippet: When hypoxia is corrected through continuous positive airway pressure ventilation, epileptic seizures are controlled in patients with OSAS, further confirming the connection between intermittent hypoxia and epilepsy

entries.proposition: The review concedes that research on hypoxia and epilepsy susceptibility is insufficient and that the hypoxia-epilepsy studies it names are mainly neonatal rodent models.
entries.snippet: Current international academic research on hypoxia and epilepsy susceptibility is insufficient.

entries.proposition: Hypoxia type matters: chronic, intermittent and acute hypoxia have different effects on excitability and age modifies them; hypoxia can also be neuroprotective in adults.
entries.snippet: Hypoxia has different effects on brain excitability at different ages.

entries.proposition: HIF-1 alpha is the shared node of the proposed mechanism: intermittent hypoxia stabilises it and it drives IL-6 and TNF-alpha.
entries.snippet: Hypoxia could upregulate HIF1-α via increasing posttranslational stabilization

entries.proposition: Neuroinflammation is described as a modulator of epilepsy and not its direct cause; anti-inflammatory treatment did not remit epilepsy in the cited work.
entries.snippet: The latest view is that neuroinflammation is not a direct cause of epilepsy, but a modulator of epilepsy and a disease-inducing factor.

entries.proposition: The conclusion calls for the missing experiment: first confirm hypoxia in epilepsy patients' sleep, then test whether resolving it reduces seizures.
entries.snippet: Next, it is necessary to investigate whether resolving intermittent hypoxia in epilepsy patients during sleep could result in a reduction of epilepsy symptoms.

entries.proposition: Three schematic figures opened: an OSAS-epilepsy loop with intermittent hypoxia driving IL-1 beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha, ROS and ER stress to brain damage and anti-inflammatory or antioxidant drugs inhibiting it; a HIF-1 alpha, NF-kB, ROS and cytokine mechanism (the nuclear box is labelled HER where the text says HRE); a synapse and ER-stress scheme with TNF-alpha, IL-1 beta, IL-6 and GRP78, PERK, IRE1, ATF6. None contains data.
